column2: A sandbender caravan moves across the dunes with an ease that seems impossible. They teach me to read shifting ground and trust balance over brute force. The desert has its own kind of strength.
Thank them, then continue my journey
In the Foggy Swamp, waterbenders guide vines and roots as though the whole forest were alive. Their strange techniques remind me that the elements are connected in ways I have yet to understand.
Thank them, then continue my journey
The Earth Kingdom is vast, and finding a teacher will take patience. I must learn to stand firm, listen to the world beneath my feet, and meet earthbending with discipline rather than force.
The Fire Nation will test my resolve. I must find a teacher who can show me how to understand fire without being consumed by its power.

The Fire Sages told me about my training.
I have to leave my own home, my Nation, my parents and friends, to see the World, to master all four elements, to become the True Avatar, to keep the balance in the Universe.
First, I will go to the Air Nomads. There I will be taught not only airbending, but meditation and concentration.
Then, to the Water Tribes. Water is the most difficult for fire avatars to master.
The Earth Kingdom is vast. Teachers are honoured there. The earth teaches strength and discipline.
After learning all the elements, I will learn to control the state of the Avatar

The Elders told me of my training. I must leave my home, my people, my friends and teachers to see the world, to master all four elements, to become a True Avatar, to keep the universe in balance. I will first go to the Water tribes. The Earth Kingdom is vast. Teachers are revered there. The Earth teaches strength and discipline. The Earth is most difficult for Airbenders to comprehend. Then I will go to the Fire Nation. After learning all the elements, I will learn how to control the Avatar state.

The Old Ones told me about my training. I must leave my home, my people, my friends and teachers to see the world, to master all four elements, to become a True Avatar, to keep the universe in balance. I will first go to the Earth Realm. The Earth Kingdom is vast. Teachers are revered there. The Earth teaches strength and discipline. Then I will go to the Fire Nation, fire is most difficult for waterbenders to learn. In the end I will spend months meditating on the peaks of the highest mountains of the Lands of Air Nomads. After learning all the elements, I will learn how to control the Avatar state.

The Old Ones told me about my training. I must leave my home, my people, my friends and teachers to see the world, to master all four elements, to become a True Avatar, to keep the universe in balance. First I will travel to the Fire Nation, where dragons live on distant islands. Then I will travel to the Air Nomads, the air is most difficult for earthbenders. At the end I will have to learn waterbending among the ice and icebergs. After learning all the elements, I will learn how to control the Avatar state.

I was already starting to pack my things, but soon the elders came and told me that I wouldn't need worldly things anymore. Before they left, they left a gift, a basket of fruit and a stack of ring-like coins. That should be enough for the journey and supplies.

I was already starting to pack my things, but soon the sages came and told me that I wouldn't need worldly things anymore. Before they left, they left a gift, a basket of fruit and a stack of coins. That should be enough for the journey and supplies.

I was already starting to pack my things, but soon the fire sages came and told me that I wouldn't need worldly things anymore. Before they left, they left a gift, a basket of fruit and a stack of knife-shaped coins. That should be enough for the journey and supplies.

I was already starting to pack my things, but soon the elders came and told me that I wouldn't need worldly things anymore. I'm only supposed to take my staff and comb. Before they left, they left a gift, a basket of fruit and a stack of coins. That should be enough for the journey and supplies.
I am very grateful, but as you said, I will no longer need worldly things.
I beg your pardon, shouldn't the Avatar be treated with more reverence?

A couple of days later, the elders came again. There wasn't much time left, and soon it would be time me to leave. They said there were several ships lined up at the port. Simple fishermen, merchants, aristocrats, and even the chief himself, wish to provide ships for the Avatar's voyage to other lands.

A couple of days later, the sages came again. There wasn't much time left, and soon it would be time me to leave. They said there was a whole line of barges and junks lined up at the port. Simple fishermen, merchants, aristocrats, and even The King himself, wish to provide ships for the Avatar's voyage to other lands.

A couple of days later, the fire sages came again. There wasn't much time left, and soon it would be time me to leave. They said there was a whole line of barges and junks lined up at the port. Simple fishermen, merchants, aristocrats, and even Firelord himself, wish to provide ships for the Avatar's voyage to other lands.

A couple of days later, the elders came again. There wasn't much time left, and soon it would be time me to leave. They say they have provided escorts for me on flying bison. I won't have to fly to the water tribes alone.
One of the Fire Lord's personal ships
Available because you are at Fire Lord's court
I decided to go on a trip to §Y[avatar_journey_target.PrimaryTitle.GetName]§! to [avatar_journey_target.GetTitledFirstName].

The Water Tribes live at the ends of the world, one in the north and one in the south. The North is a single kingdom behind a wall of ice, ruled by a chief who claims the moon's favor. Its women are taught to heal, not to fight. The South is a scatter of villages and feuding chiefdoms, poorer in ships and richer in freedom, and there a woman may learn to fight as well as heal.
I'm going to the Northern Water Tribe!
The walls of Agna Qel'a rise out of the ice before the ship has dropped anchor. Guards in blue furs meet me at the water gate and lead me through a city of canals and bridges to the chief's palace.
There is so much ice and snow here

A runner in blue furs finds me before I have brushed the salt from my coat. [northern_water_chief.GetTitledName] invites me to a feast in my honor, and the runner does not leave until I have accepted.

The feast is held in the chief's great hall. Drums sound as the guests take their seats. A whole crab is lowered into a cauldron at the center of the hall, and steam fills the rafters. When the drums stop, [northern_water_chief.GetTitledName] rises. 'Tonight we honor a guest sent by the spirits,' [northern_water_chief.GetSheHe] says. 'Avatar [GetFirstName].' The hall erupts. Before the echoes die, [northern_water_chief.GetSheHe] gestures to the far end of the table. 'And now Master [waterbending_master.GetFirstName] and [waterbending_master.GetHerHis] disciples will perform.'

At the feast I am introduced to Master [waterbending_master.GetFirstName]. [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] looks me over the way a hunter looks at a sled dog. 'Good evening, Avatar,' [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] says. 'It is an honor to teach you.' I bow. 'The honor is mine, Master.' [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] does not smile. 'Dawn, in the square. Do not be late because tonight is your feast.'
Welcome, my Avatar, it is an honor for us to receive such a guest!

I am in the square before the sun clears the wall. Master [waterbending_master.GetFirstName] is already there, running two young men through a form that makes the water in the fountain rise and fall like breath. [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] nods once when I join them. By the end of the morning my arms ache, and the form is beginning to feel less like a stranger's.

I am in the square before the sun clears the wall. Master [waterbending_master.GetFirstName] is already there, running two young men through a form that makes the water in the fountain rise and fall like breath. [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] nods once when I join them. Every time I reach for the water, fire answers instead. The fountain hisses, and the square fills with steam. The master watches without a word.
Teacher! I want to learn more about waterbending!!
The Legend of Tui and La

After the first day, Master [waterbending_master.GetFirstName] finds me at the edge of the canal. 'The moon was the first waterbender,' [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] says. 'Our ancestors watched it pull the tides and learned to pull the same way. The moon is Tui. The ocean is La. One pulls, one holds. If you learn the moon, the water will answer you.' [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] glances at the sky. 'When the moon is full, I will show you the rest.'

A few nights later, Master [waterbending_master.GetFirstName] stops me on the way to my quarters and leads me to a wooden door in the palace courtyard. Behind it is a garden, warm and green, with a pool at its center. Two fish circle each other in the water, one black and one white. 'This is the heart of the North,' [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] says. 'Every spirit in this land drinks from this pool.' The full moon is overhead, and the water is bright enough to hurt.

Master [waterbending_master.GetFirstName] sits beside the pool and gestures for me to do the same. 'You came here to learn,' [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] says. 'Not to enjoy the feast. Watch the fish. Breathe.' I watch. The black fish turns, and the white fish follows. The garden falls away. There is only the water, the moon, and the two fish. When the sun rises, my knees are stiff and my mind is quiet.
§YYou feel your understanding of waterbending has improved§!

That night I go to the shore instead of my quarters. The tide is coming in, and the moon is a thin white curve over the water. I think of the fish, the pull and the push, and raise my hands. The surf stops an arm's length from my boots, then climbs again. 'Good,' says Master [waterbending_master.GetFirstName] from behind me. I turn, startled. [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] is smiling for the first time. 'You have the basics. Dawn, as always.'
Every morning I return to the square. The master's students are waiting, and the fountain is already moving.

The students come at me one after another. The first is slow, the second is not, and by the third my arms are shaking. I hold the water longer than I thought I could, but the last student slips inside my guard and puts me on my back in the fountain. The master calls the bout. I lie there, breathless, and the water runs out of my sleeves.

The students come at me one after another. The first is slow, the second is not, and by the third my arms are shaking. But the water answers faster now. I catch the last student's wrist, turn the wave aside, and send them skidding across the wet stone. The square goes quiet. The master nods.

After I put the best apprentice on the stones, the master does not call for another student. [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] steps into the square and takes off [waterbending_master.GetHerHis] outer robe. 'Now,' [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] says, 'we will see what you have learned.'

The master moves like the tide. Every wave I throw breaks around [waterbending_master.GetHerHim], and every step I take leaves me open. I last longer than I expected. Then [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] hooks my ankle with a ribbon of water and I go down hard. [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] offers me a hand. 'Again,' [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] says.

The master moves like the tide, and for a long time I am only trying to stay upright. Then I begin to see the pattern: the same turn of the wrist before every wave, the same shift of weight before every strike. I wait. When [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] turns, I take the water out from under [waterbending_master.GetHerHim] and send it back in a single wave. The master slides across the wet stone and stops at the palace steps. [waterbending_master.GetSheHe] laughs, once, and gets up.

On the path of the Avatar, the journey to one of the Main Four Air Temples was always one of the most difficult challenges. The Air Nomads live in isolation, their major centers located on four edges of the world: In the mountains, high above the sky, and under the cliffs, where they cannot be seen from the ground.\nSometimes they can be seen in the foothill towns or on islands like Kyoshi or Itakshir, where they ask for alms, or trade, buy food, and fly away. They would welcome a fellow traveller, It would not be out of place to say that once Avatar is nominated, they are among the first to send ambassadors, they treat teaching Avatar as one of their main goals in life.\n"By ship or by foot, always move against the Wind, to the places where it is born." That was the last thing I was told.
I'll go to the Southern Temple, the greatest temple
to the Eastern Temple, to the places of the first airbenders
to the Northern Temple, where Guru Laghima was living
to the Western Temple, where Great Yangchen was born

After months of sailing, the ship entered the foggy waters of Whaletail Island. The island was always surrounded by fogs, the air here was cold from the fast sea currents of the South Sea, and only high towers of temples on the hills saved ships from eternal wandering in frosty oblivion to the inevitable crash on the reefs.\nIt was rumoured that the fogs were created here by waterbenders to prevent ships of other nations from fishing here. Others considered this a manifestation of ancient spirits, like the Spirit of Mist, as ancient as the Spirits of the Moon and the Ocean.\nAlthough the air nomads do not like to settle on the coast, the fogs protected them as well as mountains and cliffs. The island has a tradition of fasting, and every summer hundreds and thousands of air nomads go on pilgrimage to this island, where Monk Tang Xu fasted for 98 days.
Here, I think I'll find fellow travellers to the Southern Air Temple.

Hidden in the misty hills, a giant wooden temple was visible.
A tall pagoda towered over the mist, indicating to skybison the location of the temple. Near the temple there were hundreds of living quarters on stilts. Skybison slept beneath them. There was a smell of incense everywhere, the fog held the smell in the air for many hours.
The temple seemed to be divided into two parts, connected by high bridges.
And like the temple, there seemed to be two types of people.
Some in the typical yellow-orange outfits of air nomads, and others completely in dark red, they stayed away from each other.
There was a vast market square around the pagoda, where nomads from all over the world exchanged goods. And although it was difficult to measure because of the fog, it seemed that this is the most densely populated place of airnomads in the world...
I'll take a walk down to the market square

Here, they traded goods from all over the world. Famous fruit pies, whale and walrus bones, silk, paintings, oil, paper, scrolls and books. Moreover, coins of all four nations were used in the exchange. Currency exchange shops were especially successful. Natural exchange was also often used.\nIt turned out that many air nomads traded here on behalf of the Beifong house. Here was the postal center of air nomads, from ancient times, the Earth Kings hired them as messengers.\nNo one could imagine that without air nomads, the world trade would end...
It's very easy to get lost here
(In the future, there will be market options instead)

I was as if intoxicated by this hazy picture. Suddenly, a monk patted me on the shoulder. It was a young monk, a messenger from the Temple. They were notified of my arrival and took a long time to find me...\nOn the way to the temple the messenger often stopped and showed me the sights around the temple. Great cave vaporium, jade statue of Tang Xu, spring and autumn fasting square. At the entrance to the western part of the temple, decapitated statues were visible at the entrance to the eastern part. We were warmly welcomed at the temple by a group of five elders, and the messenger left. We talked about the duties of an Avatar and my training.\nI was offered to stay for a couple of days to see the Tang Xu Festival, but wouldn't it be better to fly to the Southern Air Temple as soon as possible?
Yes, I will stay for the festival

The Tang Xu Festival was much different from anything I could have imagined. Usually at festivals there is a lot of food, sound and activity. But here you were able to listen only gong banging and eat lean food.
Many people still were playing pai-sho. And a lot were seating around the pagoda meditating.
One monk called me to his pai-sho table, offered to play. "You're not from here, right?"
"I also see that you are not an airbender. Or is it no longer customary in the 'free' commune to shave your head?"
The game went on while I was telling him my story.
I want to know more about those "free" people
Are you going to the Southern Air Temple by any chance?

Long ago, when airbenders flew not on skybison and gliders, but walked on the clouds, when our nation was young and proud, and the first statue of Wang had not yet been carved, there were those who did not hesitate to encroach on someone else's life. They worshiped hungry spirits in exchange for knowledge.\nMillennia later, after a long wandering in the spirit world, Guru Liu Xi recorded the history of air nomads. Guru Laghima, Shoken, and Liu Xi's historical notes have inspired a new generation of free" folks, and the monk Tang Xu, without knowing it, found them a shelter here.\nThey eat meat and fish for Giant Koi for lamp oil. Our temple is divided into two parts, and the bridge between them will soon rot, which no one will notice. There are rumours of screams on the night of the Tang Xu festival, you won't be staying the night, are you?"
Thanks for warning, I'm leaving tomorrow.
Are you going to the Southern Air Temple by any chance?

In the middle of the night, something interrupted my sleep. After the monk's story, I already had a restless dream.\nThe wind could be heard blowing through the wooden walls.\nBut all this was drowned out by the sound of the banging on a gong. The sound pulsed in my ears, although it was relaxing, and seemed to move away.
Let's see what's going on there

I quickly and quietly dressed, left the house standing on the pillars. Hazy skies in the distance was painted red and yellow glow. The smell of incense was emitted in the same direction. The light shone in the direction of the "Free" commune. The streets were empty, was I the only one who was awakened by this?Coming closer, the gong began to complement the sonorous voices of prayers in a strange language. Not understanding the words, one could feel their antiquity, that these words were definitely not from this era.\nFollowing the sound, I went out to the square near the eastern part of the temple. Hundreds of monks in red robes sat and with closed eyes recited the mantra melodiously.\n"Would you like to join, wanderer?" said the same monk I spoke to during the day. "Soon the time of sacrifice will come, and whose voices He does not hear, He will take with Him."
May lead to a change of religion on the island or death!

I don't know why, but I froze. I heard, through the prayers and the gong, the monk was saying something, his lips were moving, but I heard only This. As through the fog, as through the water, something was moving. I just noticed that the monk was talking with his eyes closed. Suddenly, he gave up his attempts, and sat down in his place, repeating the words of the ancients.\nThe sound of movement grew more and more, and a flying fish swam out of the forest. I felt a look on me, heavy and light at the same time.\nWhat am I doing here? What should I do? Is it a spirit? What kind of sacrifice? So many thoughts were running through my head. And something unlimited seemed to take control over me, something so familiar that it didn't take words to describe it. This was the first Avatar State.
I feel the power and the will... The whisper of forgotten Avatars tells me to end the madness, maybe even at the cost of my own oblivion
I hear the voice no one able to hear... I can speak the language no one able to speak but someone before me, I can speak it, talk to This

Taking the Thing by surprise, I unleashed upon him all the power and wrath of the Avatars he once carried away.\nWhen I woke up, I saw a destroyed forest. Suddenly, the monks lost hundreds of years ago came out of the fog, the monks sitting in shock came to their senses and helped their people get out of the forest. The fog began to dissipate, rise and collect in large clouds. Soon the clouds flew away in an unknown direction.\nEven if the spirit is not destroyed, it will not soon disturb these places again.

Hundreds of Avatars have seen this spirit before me. I feel their anger. Spirit feels it too. The fog is thickening, there is pitch darkness.
A strong blow, possibly a tail. Dozens of broken tree branches behind. With high speed, it is behind the trunk.
Hit.
I can't feel the body. Forces go somewhere. The light goes out. Where are you going? Why are you leaving me at the most important moment?
Hit.
Abandoned even by own past lives...

Today we fly to the Southern Air Temple. We packed in a bison saddle, and I took one last look at the foggy hills of Whaletail Island. [fellow_traveler.GetFirstName] took the reins, and said yip-yip. His skybison [GetSkybisonName] kicked off the ground with its tail and we soared into the air. Very quickly we emerged from the blinding vapors, turns out they were not just fogs bug fallen clouds.\nFog look so soft from here, like you could just jump down and you'd land in a big, soft, cottony heap. There where the clouds dropped to the ground, and seemed like fogs, I missed the Sun so much. Signal tower and lighthouses sweep below, soon the blue of the sea began to be seen, and I calmed down. The waters were calm too.

We have crossed the Patola ridges and should be arriving at the Southern Air Temple soon.\nMountain peaks began to cut through the clouds, and in the distance could be seen the Great Temple, the Southern Air Temple.\nYoung monks were flying around, some of them playing air polo

[fellow_traveler.GetFirstName] began to lead the bison to land.
As soon as we descended, five elders approached the bison. They bowed and the central one said: "It is a great honour for us to welcome you. We are the elders of this temple.
We and our best teachers will teach you airbending and our traditions."
Then they escorted me to my monastery cell.
After a long flight, I was very tired and fell asleep quickly

I lived in the same room with several other monks. Gyatso was the most powerful airbender among us. We quickly hit it off. Gyatso was younger than me, but definitely wiser than many in the Fire Nation. Like other airbenders, he was not deprived of a sense of humor. For the first time since my separation from Sozin, I stopped feeling lonely.
It's nice to have a friend

Gyatso was assigned as my guide and told to give me a tour of the Temple. I was shown dozens of prayer rooms and gardens. There is no large-scale production here and it is not customary to wear luxury.
It turned out that huge networks of underground corridors were dug under the Temple.
There they extract special blue crystals that are ground into dust and applied under the skin when tattooing.
Finally, we went to the main tower. There is a sanctuary there, only the elders and the Avatar can enter. Massive wooden gates with a complex system of pipes can only be opened by airbending masters.

Today we have been meditating all day. The monks say that air is the element of freedom. So the first step to understanding it is to free your mind. We sat in a circle and concentrated on our breathing. The aim of the exercise was to become aware of the most basic thing in the airbending: the process of breathing, to feel how air inhales, spreads over the body, and exhales freely.

Before conquering the air, I need to feel the balance. Today we practised balance on high and thin poles all day. I fell down many times, but the teachers helped me again and again. Many airbenders did not have much difficulty, many were meditating

After weeks of meditation and balance training, my next challenge will be walking through dozens of spinning gates. The monks say that the secret of this exercise is to liken oneself to a leaf in the wind. It teaches circular movements and overcoming obstacles without the use of force.

After many weeks of training, I finally passed the test. It was difficult, but now I am free to get through the gates at any speed. It's like a dance, not without a reason airbenders are so good at dancing.

I haven't been able to get through this gate for weeks. I can't even make it a third of the way through, I keep getting hit and thrown out every time. The monks are reassuring, they say it's a difficult exercise and not all avatars pass it quickly.

It was the first time I had airbended! After months of training, I'm finally flying through the clouds. The group and I were transported to the highest peak, from where I was told to take off in a glider. I thought it was crazy and I couldn't handle it, and I refused for a long time, but the teachers insisted that if anything happened, they would rescue me. Only when I got off the ground did I finally feel real freedom, and the air obeyed me.

At last I can open the gate to the sanctuary. The monks say that only elders and avatars can open them. Opening them with an airbending, I entered the dark room. Walking a little further, I saw statues of past avatars: Kyoshi, Kuruk, Jangchen, Szeto, Salai... I don't know how, but just looking at them fills me with wisdom.
I had finished mastering airbending. The monks blessed me and provided me with a sky bison escort to the water tribes. I'm going to miss this temple...

A messenger from the Beifong estates arrives with an elegant, sturdy vessel, its crew proud to serve one of the Earth Kingdom's most influential families. Their offer is generous, but accepting it would mean owing a favor to a house whose reach extends far beyond Gaoling.

A delegation from Omashu offers a broad, well-built trade barge. Its captain boasts that the city's ingenious merchants can get cargo and important passengers through almost any port. The ship is practical, dependable, and unmistakably Omashu in spirit.

Royal envoys from Ba Sing Se arrive bearing the Earth King's offer: a guarded vessel, polished fittings, and a crew chosen for the royal voyage. Accepting would be the most prestigious way to travel, but the ship's banners would make it clear that the Earth King's court has taken an interest in your journey.

After a long journey south, I reach the Southern Water Tribe. The chief meets me at the gate and promises to find a teacher. The village is smaller than I expected, a ring of tents and low ice houses around a frozen harbor. Children follow me through the snow, and no one bows.
Meet the Southern Water Tribe's waterbenders

The first sparring lesson is harder than I expected. Every stance I learned from the earth tells me to plant my feet and take the hit. The water does not care. It goes around my guard, under my feet, and I end up on my back in the fountain. The master says nothing. I get up.

When I reach the Fire Nation, Sozin greets me with the easy familiarity of an old friend. With a mischievous grin, he lifts an ornate ceremonial crown and places it on my head, declaring that for one day I should rule over him. The gesture is playful, but beneath the joke is a reminder of the bond we share before duty and ambition pull our lives in different directions.
Accept the crown in the spirit of friendship
